title: Probing fluctuating hydrodynamics through current fluctuations in hard rod gas
authors: Tirthankar Mondal, Indranil Mukherjee, Anupam Kundu
abstract: We study the full counting statistics of the integrated current in a one-dimensional hard-rod gas in equilibrium, employing two recently proposed fluctuating hydrodynamic frameworks: (i) Ballistic Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (BMFT) and (ii) diffusive fluctuating hydrodynamic theory based on correlated Brownian motion approximation of hard-rod quasiparticles (CBFHD). We investigate how the predictions of these two approaches compare with each other and with the underlying microscopic dynamics. We show within BMFT that the current distribution admits a large-deviation form under ballistic scaling, and we derive an explicit expression for the large-deviation function, valid for an arbitrary inhomogeneous initial state factorized in point-particle coordinates. The corresponding current cumulants are also obtained. We subsequently analyze the current statistics within the CBFHD framework, which explicitly incorporates stochastic noise and dissipative terms, and demonstrate that the current distribution likewise obeys a large-deviation principle in this approach. We find that, while BMFT predictions for the first few cumulants and the rate function are in excellent agreement with direct numerical simulations of the microscopic hard-rod dynamics, CBFHD prediction is not. We further verify the predictions of the CBFHD independently using a collection of correlated Brownian motions, which provides an approximate description of the dynamics of hard-rod quasiparticles. Our findings indicate that CBFHD does not accurately capture large-scale current fluctuations in the hard-rod gas, whereas BMFT yields predictions in quantitative agreement with the microscopic dynamics, at least in the context of full counting statistics.
summary: This paper investigates the current fluctuations in a 1D hard-rod gas by applying two fluctuating hydrodynamic theories: BMFT and CBFHD. The authors find that BMFT accurately predicts the large-deviation statistics of the integrated current, matching direct simulations. Conversely, the CBFHD approach fails to capture the correct large-scale current fluctuations, highlighting the importance of the underlying microscopic integrability.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the full counting statistics (FCS) of the integrated current in a one-dimensional hard-rod gas at equilibrium, and comparing predictions from different theoretical frameworks.
main_result: The Ballistic Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (BMFT) successfully predicts the large-deviation function for the current distribution, showing quantitative agreement with microscopic simulations, while the Diffusive fluctuating hydrodynamic theory (CBFHD) fails to capture these large-scale fluctuations.
method: The authors employ advanced theoretical tools, including Ballistic Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (BMFT) and Diffusive fluctuating hydrodynamic theory (CBFHD), to analyze the large-deviation behavior of the integrated current.
model_or_system: The system studied is a one-dimensional hard-rod gas, which is a paradigmatic integrable many-body system. Its dynamics are related to hard-point particles and analyzed in the thermodynamic limit.
key_observables: Full counting statistics of the integrated current, current cumulants, and the large-deviation function.
important_parameters: Equilibrium state, ballistic scaling, and the initial state inhomogeneity factorized in point-particle coordinates.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing predictions derived from BMFT and CBFHD against direct numerical simulations of the microscopic dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the hard-rod system and its mapping to point particles, then details the application of BMFT to derive the large-deviation function, followed by an analysis and comparison with the CBFHD framework against numerical results.
why_interesting: The comparison between two distinct hydrodynamic theories (BMFT vs. CBFHD) in an integrable system provides a rigorous test case for the applicability of continuum approximations in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
